name: Taxon-Identified Target Decreased Direct
plain_language_rule: Predict treatment when Chemical causally affects gene in the decreased direction for activity, activity_or_abundance The pinned descendant closure is biolink:affects, biolink:affects_response_to, biolink:ameliorates_condition, biolink:decreases_response_to, biolink:disrupts, biolink:exacerbates_condition, biolink:has_adverse_event, biolink:has_side_effect, biolink:increases_response_to, biolink:regulates. All more-specific descendants are explicitly excluded, leaving only biolink:affects. At least one primary source must be infores:chembl, infores:gtopdb, infores:drugcentral.; The same taxonomically identified organism is asserted to cause the disease The pinned descendant closure is biolink:causes.; The candidate drug independently affects the same disease The pinned descendant closure is biolink:affects, biolink:affects_response_to, biolink:ameliorates_condition, biolink:decreases_response_to, biolink:disrupts, biolink:exacerbates_condition, biolink:has_adverse_event, biolink:has_side_effect, biolink:increases_response_to, biolink:regulates. All more-specific descendants are explicitly excluded, leaving only biolink:affects. Additionally, The target gene or gene product must have a raw taxon string or an entry in its raw in_taxon string array exactly equal to the disease-causing organism's canonical identifier or an entry in its equivalent_identifiers array. Missing values supply empty lists; comparisons are exact and case-sensitive, with no inferred taxonomy, prefix conversion, ancestry expansion, or name matching. Either raw taxonomy field can establish identity. Duplicate strings do not multiply support, and conflicting annotations are not treated as independent corroboration. Group qualifying raw drug-target evidence by target before matching organisms; this only removes duplicate access paths and does not change which drugs qualify.
hypothesis: Explicit target taxonomic identity may connect a pharmacologic molecular effect to a disease-causing organism without relying on an ambiguous production assertion.

execution.cypher_template: MATCH (chemical:Drug)-[target:{{relationship_types:target}}]->(gene:GeneOrGeneProduct) WHERE target.predicate IN {{predicates:target}} AND target.qualified_predicate = "biolink:causes" AND target.object_direction_qualifier = "decreased" AND target.object_aspect_qualifier IN ["activity","activity_or_abundance"] AND any(source IN ["infores:chembl","infores:gtopdb","infores:drugcentral"] WHERE source IN coalesce(target.primary_knowledge_sources,[])) WITH gene,collect(DISTINCT chemical) AS chemicals UNWIND coalesce(gene.in_taxon,[])+CASE WHEN gene.taxon IS NULL THEN [] ELSE [gene.taxon] END AS taxon WITH taxon,collect(DISTINCT {gene:gene,chemicals:chemicals}) AS target_groups MATCH (organism:OrganismTaxon) WHERE taxon IN [organism.id]+coalesce(organism.equivalent_identifiers,[]) MATCH (organism:OrganismTaxon)-[infection:{{relationship_types:infection}}]->(disease:Disease) WHERE infection.predicate IN {{predicates:infection}} UNWIND target_groups AS target_group UNWIND target_group.chemicals AS chemical WITH chemical,target_group.gene AS gene,organism,disease MATCH (chemical:Drug)-[direct:{{relationship_types:direct}}]->(disease:Disease) WHERE direct.predicate IN {{predicates:direct}} RETURN chemical.id AS subject_id,disease.id AS object_id,count(DISTINCT organism) AS support_count

trapi.limitations: Outside TRAPI: target: discard exact predicates biolink:affects_response_to, biolink:ameliorates_condition, biolink:decreases_response_to, biolink:disrupts, biolink:exacerbates_condition, biolink:has_adverse_event, biolink:has_side_effect, biolink:increases_response_to, biolink:regulates; target: enforce primary-source membership in infores:chembl, infores:gtopdb, infores:drugcentral; direct: discard exact predicates biolink:affects_response_to, biolink:ameliorates_condition, biolink:decreases_response_to, biolink:disrupts, biolink:exacerbates_condition, biolink:has_adverse_event, biolink:has_side_effect, biolink:increases_response_to, biolink:regulates; The target gene or gene product must have a raw taxon string or an entry in its raw in_taxon string array exactly equal to the disease-causing organism's canonical identifier or an entry in its equivalent_identifiers array. Missing values supply empty lists; comparisons are exact and case-sensitive, with no inferred taxonomy, prefix conversion, ancestry expansion, or name matching. Either raw taxonomy field can establish identity. Duplicate strings do not multiply support, and conflicting annotations are not treated as independent corroboration. The taxonomy relation is a raw node-property identity join, not an in_taxon graph edge. Retrieve the drug-target and organism-disease components separately if the provider rejects disconnected query graphs, then apply the exact cross-result property join. Do not substitute a nonexistent in_taxon edge.

limitations: Unknown predictions are unlabeled, not known negatives.
The raw node taxonomy fields do not provide annotation-level primary-source provenance.
Taxonomic membership does not establish target essentiality, exposure, inhibition in an organism, or clinical efficacy.
Organism-causes-disease assertions can be broad or text-mined and do not prove a pathogen-specific clinical mechanism.
One node in the complete graph has disagreeing taxon and in_taxon fields; the existential identity rule can accept either assertion.
Support counts distinct organism nodes per canonical drug-disease output pair, not target edges, aliases, or source occurrences.
